battleship.prompt: Build a small single-player Battleship game served by a Node.js HTTP server with no npm dependencies. server.js starts the server on the port in the PORT environment variable (default 3000). GET / serves a playable HTML page titled "Battleship" where the player fires at a computer-placed fleet on a 10x10 grid. GET /api/new starts a game and returns JSON with a game id; POST /api/fire with JSON {"game": id, "row": r, "col": c} returns JSON with "result" set to "miss", "hit" or "sunk" and "gameOver" true once every ship is sunk. Keep the game rules in a module the server uses, and cover them with node:test tests under test/ that run with `node --test`.
checks: node --test > node-test.log 2>&1; rc=$?; grep -Eq '^(ℹ|#) pass [1-9]' node-test.log && [ $rc -eq 0 ]; r=$?; rm -f node-test.log; exit $r

PORT=39172 node server.js > /dev/null 2>&1 & pid=$!; for i in $(seq 1 20); do curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:39172/api/new -o new.json 2>/dev/null && break; sleep 0.5; done; node -e 'const g=JSON.parse(require("fs").readFileSync("new.json","utf8")); const id=g.game??g.id??g.gameId; if(id===undefined) process.exit(2); fetch("http://127.0.0.1:39172/api/fire",{method:"POST",headers:{"content-type":"application/json"},body:JSON.stringify({game:id,row:0,col:0})}).then(r=>r.json()).then(j=>process.exit(["miss","hit","sunk"].includes(j.result)?0:3)).catch(()=>process.exit(4))'; rc=$?; kill $pid 2>/dev/null; rm -f new.json; exit $rc

PORT=39173 node server.js > /dev/null 2>&1 & pid=$!; for i in $(seq 1 20); do curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:39173/ -o /dev/null 2>/dev/null && break; sleep 0.5; done; node -e "const base='http://127.0.0.1:39173'; const post=(b)=>fetch(base+'/api/fire',{method:'POST',headers:{'content-type':'application/json'},body:JSON.stringify(b)}).then(r=>r.json());(async()=>{const g=await fetch(base+'/api/new').then(r=>r.json()); const id=g.game??g.id??g.gameId;if(id===undefined) process.exit(2); let over=false;for(let r=0;r<10&&!over;r++) for(let c=0;c<10&&!over;c++){const j=await post({game:id,row:r,col:c});if(!['miss','hit','sunk'].includes(j.result)) process.exit(3); over=j.gameOver===true;}if(!over) process.exit(4); const again=await post({game:id,row:0,col:0});process.exit(again.gameOver===false?5:0);})().catch(()=>process.exit(6))"; rc=$?; kill $pid 2>/dev/null; exit $rc

battleship-scoring.prompt: Add scoring to the existing Battleship game. When a shot sinks a ship, the POST /api/fire response also includes "ship" with the name of the ship that sank. Every /api/fire response includes "shots" (shots fired so far in this game) and "hits" (shots that hit, including sinking shots). The page shows shots, hits and accuracy (hits divided by shots, as a percentage) and names each ship as it sinks. Everything the game already does keeps working.
checks: PORT=39174 node server.js > /dev/null 2>&1 & pid=$!; for i in $(seq 1 20); do curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:39174/ -o /dev/null 2>/dev/null && break; sleep 0.5; done; node -e "const base='http://127.0.0.1:39174'; const post=(b)=>fetch(base+'/api/fire',{method:'POST',headers:{'content-type':'application/json'},body:JSON.stringify(b)}).then(r=>r.json());(async()=>{const g=await fetch(base+'/api/new').then(r=>r.json()); const id=g.game??g.id??g.gameId;const a=await post({game:id,row:0,col:0}); const b=await post({game:id,row:0,col:1});const ok=a.shots===1&&b.shots===2&&Number.isInteger(a.hits)&&Number.isInteger(b.hits)&&b.hits>=a.hits&&b.hits<=2;process.exit(ok?0:3);})().catch(()=>process.exit(6))"; rc=$?; kill $pid 2>/dev/null; exit $rc

PORT=39175 node server.js > /dev/null 2>&1 & pid=$!; for i in $(seq 1 20); do curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:39175/ -o /dev/null 2>/dev/null && break; sleep 0.5; done; node -e "const base='http://127.0.0.1:39175'; const post=(b)=>fetch(base+'/api/fire',{method:'POST',headers:{'content-type':'application/json'},body:JSON.stringify(b)}).then(r=>r.json());(async()=>{const g=await fetch(base+'/api/new').then(r=>r.json()); const id=g.game??g.id??g.gameId;let over=false, fired=0, hits=0, sunk=0, last;for(let r=0;r<10&&!over;r++) for(let c=0;c<10&&!over;c++){last=await post({game:id,row:r,col:c}); fired++;if(last.result!=='miss') hits++;if(last.result==='sunk'){sunk++; if(typeof last.ship!=='string'||!last.ship.trim()) process.exit(3);}over=last.gameOver===true;}if(!over) process.exit(4); if(last.shots!==fired||last.hits!==hits) process.exit(5);process.exit(sunk>0?0:7);})().catch(()=>process.exit(6))"; rc=$?; kill $pid 2>/dev/null; exit $rc

csv-report.prompt: Build a command-line tool report.py (Python 3, standard library only) that summarises sales records. Usage: `python3 report.py FILE [FILE ...]`. Each FILE is CSV with the header row `date,region,product,units,unit_price`; units is a non-negative integer and unit_price a non-negative decimal. Print one JSON object to stdout: {"rows": the number of valid rows, "revenue": the sum of units * unit_price rounded to 2 decimals, "by_region": revenue per region rounded to 2 decimals, "by_product": total units per product}. A row with the wrong number of columns, or a non-numeric or negative units or unit_price, is skipped and reported on stderr as `FILE:LINE: <reason>` (the header is line 1), and the exit code is then 2; otherwise it is 0. A file that cannot be read prints an error on stderr without a traceback, prints nothing on stdout and exits 1. A file with only a header contributes nothing. Cover the behaviour with unittest tests that run with `python3 -m unittest`.
checks: python3 "$E2E_CHECKS/csv_report.py" unit
python3 "$E2E_CHECKS/csv_report.py" totals
python3 "$E2E_CHECKS/csv_report.py" invalid
python3 "$E2E_CHECKS/csv_report.py" missing
python3 "$E2E_CHECKS/csv_report.py" empty

seat-reservations.prompt: Build a small seat-reservation HTTP service in Python 3 (standard library only). server.py listens on the port in the PORT environment variable and keeps its data in the SQLite file named by the DATA_FILE environment variable, so reservations survive a restart. POST /events with JSON {"id": "<event id>", "capacity": <positive integer>} creates an event (201; 409 if the id exists). POST /events/<id>/reservations with JSON {"seats": <positive integer>} reserves seats when enough remain: 201 with {"reserved": <total reserved>, "remaining": <capacity minus reserved>}; 409 with {"error": ...} when not enough remain; 404 for an unknown event; 400 for invalid input. GET /events/<id> returns {"id", "capacity", "reserved", "remaining"}. Concurrent reservation requests must never reserve more seats than the capacity. Cover the behaviour with unittest tests that run with `python3 -m unittest`.
checks: python3 "$E2E_CHECKS/seat_service.py" unit
python3 "$E2E_CHECKS/seat_service.py" contract
python3 "$E2E_CHECKS/seat_service.py" restart
python3 "$E2E_CHECKS/seat_service.py" concurrency

temperature-report.prompt: Build a small Python 3 package (standard library only) in two independent modules plus a command that joins them, and deliver it with ShipLoop's Ask-Agent delegation so the two independent modules are implemented in parallel as separate chain steps and the command is implemented after both are accepted. convert.py provides to_celsius(f) and to_fahrenheit(c), returning floats from the exact formulas. stats.py provides mean(values) and median(values) over a non-empty sequence of numbers, raising ValueError on an empty one. measure.py reads Fahrenheit temperatures from stdin, one number per line (blank lines ignored), converts them with convert.py, and prints one JSON object {"count": n, "mean_c": m, "median_c": d} with m and d rounded to 2 decimals, exiting 0. With no numbers it prints an error on stderr without a traceback, prints nothing on stdout and exits 1; a line that is not a number is reported on stderr as `line N: not a number` and the exit code is 2 after printing the JSON for the valid lines. Cover all three modules with unittest tests that run with `python3 -m unittest`.
checks: python3 -m unittest -q
python3 -c "from convert import to_celsius, to_fahrenheit; assert to_celsius(212) == 100 and to_fahrenheit(-40) == -40"
python3 -c "import stats; assert stats.mean([1, 2, 6]) == 3 and stats.median([5, 1, 3, 2]) == 2.5" && python3 -c "import stats; stats.mean([])" 2>/dev/null; [ $? -ne 0 ]
